fullText: Kya tumhe bhi yahi lagta hai? Python language ka naam Python snake se relate karte hue rakha hai? But ye kahin bhi sahi nahi hai. Baat thi 1989 ki. Jahan par ek researcher Guido van Rossum ek aisi language chahta tha joki C se zyada fast ho, simple ho. Wahi usi time apni Christmas ki chuttiyon mein ek hobby project start karta hai. Jismein wo decide karta hai, Main ek aisi language par work karunga joki C se zyada fast ho aur efficient ho. Aur usne is language ka naam rakha ek British comedy show se relate karte hue joki tha, Monty Python's Flying Circus. Isi ke naam par usne apni language ka naam rakha Python. Ye Python language ek itna bada invention hai, joki machine learning, artificial intelligence, automation jaise sectors mein kaafi important role play karti hai. Socho, ek us purane time ka chhota sa invention, jiski wajah se, aaj kitna bada ecosystem ban chuka hai.

sceneDelivery.reason: A confrontational kinetic-type cold open: PYTHON assembles letter by letter while a coiled line-art serpent and a huge question mark establish the assumption.
The serpent is visually connected to Python, then the connection breaks and a decisive NOT THE SNAKE correction replaces it.
A monumental date emerges from a moving archival timeline; no unrelated historical imagery.
A custom researcher identity card and code blueprint introduce Guido; FAST and SIMPLE become the two design requirements.
A cinematic 2.5D winter workspace: snow beyond the window, warm practical lights and a laptop where a side project runs for the first time.
An original Three.js metallic code core assembles from wireframe to solid while FAST and EFFICIENT lock into orbit.
The technical world gives way to a custom retro theatre: curtains open, marquee bulbs illuminate and the comedy-show title takes the stage.
A direct visual match: MONTY PYTHON collapses to a single glowing PYTHON nameplate and original two-colour Python-inspired mark.
One small origin node branches into an increasingly dense connected system, making ‘how big an invention’ visible rather than literal.
Three synchronized custom infographics: a neural graph for ML, a living processor for AI and an articulated robotic arm for automation.
The tiny origin cube returns, then grows into a luminous Three.js ecosystem globe surrounded by the three fields and a 1989-to-today arc.
